extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and applicants for RPG mechanisms (R01, R03, R15, R21, R34)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and reviewer guidance for assessing Research Project Grant applications (R01, R03, R15, R21, R34), including the standard review criteria and mechanism-specific considerations used to assign overall impact and criterion scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R15 variant: Reviewers will provide an overall impact/priority score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to make an important scientific contribution, to provide research opportunities to students, and to strengthen the research environment of the institution, in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: R03 (Small Research Grant) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The R03 small grant supports discrete, well-defined projects that can realistically be completed in two years with limited funding; applications may not contain extensive detail or discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the research is limited, reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach. Appropriate justification can be provided via literature citations, data from other sources, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, particularly for pilot or feasibility studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 (AREA) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives of the R15 program are to support meritorious research, strengthen research environments of schools with limited NIH support, and expose undergraduate and graduate students to research; preliminary data are not required but may be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider whether, if funded, the AREA award will substantially strengthen the research environment and expose students to research. Preliminary data optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 (Exploratory/Developmental) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: R21 supports investigation of novel ideas, new model systems, tools, or technologies with potential for significant impact; applications need not have extensive background or preliminary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will focus evaluation on conceptual framework, level of innovation, and potential to advance knowledge. Appropriate justification can be literature citations, other-source data, or investigator data when available. Preliminary data are not required but may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: R34 (Clinical Trial Planning) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: R34 supports development of Phase III clinical trials, including team establishment, data management/oversight tools, recruitment strategies, protocol finalization, and operations/procedures manual preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The R34 is not designed for collection of preliminary data or pilot studies to support trial rationale. Reviewers will focus evaluation on the rationale for the proposed clinical trial and the design/protocol in its current, early form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will completion change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive the field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R15 variant adds: If funded, will the AREA award have a substantial effect on the school/academic component in strengthening the research environment and exposing students to research?

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If Early Stage Investigators or in early independent careers, do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that advanced their field(s)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If collaborative or multi-PD/PI, do investigators have complementary and integrated expertise; are leadership, governance, and organizational structure appropriate? R15 variant adds: Do PD(s)/PI(s) have suitable experience in supervising students in research?

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the concepts, approaches, methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions are novel to one field or novel in a broad sense, or whether a refinement, improvement, or new application is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented? If early stage, will the strategy establish feasibility and manage risky aspects?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, evaluate plans to address (1) protection of human subjects from research risks, and (2) inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on basis of sex/gender, race, and ethnicity, and inclusion (or exclusion) of children, justified in terms of scientific goals and strategy. R15 variant language uses 'clinical research' and explicitly mentions inclusion of minorities and both sexes/genders. Also R15 asks whether application provides sufficient evidence that the project can stimulate student interest toward biomedical/behavioral science careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Are institutional support, equipment and other physical resources available to investigators adequate for the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Will the project benefit from unique features of the scientific environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements? R15 variant: Does the application demonstrate likely availability of well-qualified students to participate and provide evidence that students have pursued or are likely to pursue careers in biomedical/behavioral sciences?

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For research involving human subjects (non-exempt), the committee will evaluate the justification for involvement and proposed protections from research risk according to five review criteria: 1) risk to subjects, 2) adequacy of protection against risks, 3) potential benefits to the subjects and others, 4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and 5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For research that meets exemption criteria, the committee will evaluate: 1) justification for the exemption, 2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and 3) sources of materials. See Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When the project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, the committee will evaluate proposed plans for inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on the basis of sex/gender, race, and ethnicity, as well as inclusion (or exclusion) of children to determine if justified in terms of the scientific goals and research strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate involvement of live vertebrate animals according to five points: 1) proposed use and details (species, strains, ages, sex, numbers), 2) justifications for use and appropriateness of species/numbers, 3) adequacy of veterinary care, 4) procedures for limiting discomfort/distress/pain including use of analgesics/anesthetics or restraint, and 5) methods of euthanasia and reason if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If needed, determine whether adequate protection, biosafety, biocontainment, and procedures are proposed to mitigate hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: For resubmissions, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess adequacy of responses to prior critiques and whether revisions address previous concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: For renewals, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate achievements relative to original aims and justification for continued support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: For revisions, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the revision relates to a specific line of investigation from the original application that was not recommended for approval, consider whether responses to prior review comments are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries and either are not readily available in the United States or augment existing U.S. resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider unique advantages attributable to foreign location or resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information provided in the Select Agent section of the application, including the Select Agent(s) to be used, registration status of all entities where they will be used, procedures to monitor possession/use/transfer, and plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security of the Select Agent(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate completeness and adequacy of plans for safe handling, monitoring, and security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the following Resource Sharing Plans, or the rationale for not sharing, are reasonable: 1) Data Sharing Plan, 2) Sharing Model Organisms, and 3) Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS)/Genomic Data Sharing Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether plans or rationales are appropriate and sufficient given the proposed research and community norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate cost realism, justification of budget items, and whether requested duration aligns with aims and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section to offer constructive suggestions, identify critical weaknesses, or advise on whether major revisions are needed before resubmission.
